usage_note: Literally "be well": the everyday greeting for both hello and goodbye. It is said with the palms pressed together at the chest and a slight bow, the ນົບ (nop).
notes: A5 first note. ນົບ checked on English Wiktionary (verb: salute with palms pressed together); not in words.csv.

usage_note: Rice, and by extension a meal: ກິນເຂົ້າ (gin kao, "eat rice") means "have a meal". The general word for food is ອາຫານ (aa-haan).
notes: A5 first note. ກິນ (W000018) and ອາຫານ (W000028) are in words.csv; ກິນເຂົ້າ is not a row of its own.

usage_note: Lao says what you are hungry for: ຫິວເຂົ້າ (literally "hungry for rice", that is, for a meal) is how you say "hungry", and ຫິວນ້ຳ means "thirsty". A native speaker tells us that "I'm hungry" with ຫິວ alone sounds unfinished: hungry for what?
notes: PLAN L1d (c). Native speaker 2026-11-13 (via owner): bare ຂ້ອຍຫິວ sounds incomplete; say ຫິວເຂົ້າ / ຫິວນ້ຳ. ຫິວນ້ຳ vs ຢາກນ້ຳ for 'thirsty' still asked in QUESTIONS. Wording by agent. No respellings in the text (LESSON_RULES 13, curriculum review).
